newsitem.title: MOROCCO: French firm to invest $1.0 bln in Morocco.
newsitem.headline: French firm to invest $1.0 bln in Morocco.

text.p: French firm Lyonnaise des Eaux proposed on Thursday investing $1.0 billion over a 30-year period in Morocco's financial centre of Casablanca to upgrade its water and electricity networks.

Casablanca city council is negotiating with the French firm to take over management of water, electricity and public waste systems from 1997 to 2027. The city council is soon to sign the deal, officials said.

"The modernisation of Casablanca's water and electricity networks is an urgent necessity...The Lyonnaise des Eaux will invest the equivalent of $1.0 billion during a 30-year concession," Gerard Payen, head of Lyonnaise des Eaux told reporters.
The firm will be engaged in long-term development of electricity and water projects to meet consumers' increasing demands, Payen said. Casablanca has a population of more than four million.
The Lyonnaise des Eaux news conference was a reaction to Moroccan critics who warn of higher water and electricity costs under the concession, a market analyst said.
The Casablanca-based Confederation Generale des Entrepreprises du Maroc said consumers would end up paying most of Lyonnaise des Eaux expected total investment of 30 billion dirhams ($3.26 billion).
The French firm said it will invest a third of the amount while the remainder will be paid by consumers. It also said costs would rise "at no more than an average 10 percent per year."
